I moved `_task_ceiling_s` into a new module, `src/hpc_bridge/ceilings.py`, and committed it on `1b/t4-move-1790182067` as `15aaa25`. Nothing was pushed. Unit tests pass (552 passed, 2 skipped), and ruff and mypy are clean.

- **The move:** the function body is unchanged. `config.py` keeps `from .ceilings import _task_ceiling_s` so existing imports still work. That line sits at the bottom of the file with `# noqa: E402, F401`, because ruff would otherwise flag it as a late or unused import.
- **Circular import:** the function uses four names that stay in `config.py` (`_parse_hhmmss`, `SYNC_WAIT_S`, `TASK_CEILING_MARGIN_S`, `max_task_s`). So `ceilings.py` imports from `config`, and `config` imports back from `ceilings`. My first version failed with an `ImportError` when `hpc_bridge.ceilings` was imported before `config`. The fix was to put the `from .config import …` line in `ceilings.py` *after* the function, with a comment explaining why. I checked that all five modules involved import cleanly in either order.
- **Vault notes:** the livedocs gate flagged three notes whose links to the function broke, plus one more that references `config.py` as a file.
  - I updated `Modules/server.md` and `Modules/config.md` to say where the function now lives, and re-stamped them.
  - I left the two dated review notes (`Review 2026-09-03 — bugs.md` and `Review 2 2026-09-03 — code quality.md`) unedited as historical records, and acked them with a reason.
  - `Review 2026-09-03 — code quality.md` also needed acking; its text is still accurate as history.
  - The gate auto-acked six other notes as unaffected.

I did not create a `Modules/ceilings.md` note, even though the vault documents each module in its own note; say if you want one. `docs/hpc-bridge-vault/.livedocs/cache/precommit.jsonl` was already deleted when I started, and the commit hook recreated it. It now shows as modified, and I left it out of the commit.

The claude.ai Booking.com, Kiwi.com, Tripadvisor and lastminute.com connectors need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings, and the Cloudflare plugin servers need `/mcp`. The `endpoint` and `local-websearch` MCP servers failed to connect. None of them were needed for this task.
